1:_: [1] [Levush] It is not reshut harabbim, etc. And regarding when one throws from reshut hayachid to reshut harabbim — the Taz distinguishes between open to reshut harabbim where many push into it that he is not liable; see there, and from Beit Chadash and Magen Avraham it appears that in every case he is liable; and see beginning of siman 345:
2:_: [2] [Levush] A mashehu from here, etc. In Shulchan Aruch he wrote a tefach from here — meaning the remainder of the wall is less than a pas with a mashehu, and this is per the second answer of Tosafos Eruvin daf 10; and the Levush's view appears as the first answer there that even in a wall a mashehu suffices, and so it appears in Avodat HaKodesh daf 6, and Rashba should be relied upon for his ruling, and not as Bach who was strict even in pasin with a tefach and relied on R' Yehonatan — but this is not so, for even R' Yehonatan only said so regarding a wall, and even regarding a wall one can say he did not mean it literally as Beit Yosef wrote that a mashehu suffices:
3:_: [3] There is not in the breach 4 tefachim, etc. And it is possible he speaks of a courtyard wide in the middle and at its end it is narrow so that in its full width there is not 4 tefachim; but if the entire courtyard is less than 4 tefachim no repair is needed as written in seif 21 (Magen Avraham), and it is not clear — for there he speaks of a mavo but in a courtyard repair is needed as explained in Eruvin daf 12, and so it appears in Mordechai and Agudah and Hagahot Alfasi there. For tzurat hapetach see siman 362 seif 10:
4:_: [4] [Levush] All that it is. Even less than a finger (Beit Yosef):
5:_: [5] If one tied a person there, etc. He speaks where they did not inform him — if so he will leave from there, therefore it requires being tied (Magen Avraham), and see siman 362 s.k. 11:
6:_: [6] [Levush] And specifically in the repair, etc. And from Levush Yom Tov he answered that two sides are different; and see s.k. 2:
7:_: [7] Cannot stand, etc. And even if the wind does not knock it down but only shakes it as explained at the beginning of siman 362 (Magen Avraham):
8:_: [8] Distant, etc. For the air of this side comes and nullifies it — therefore if the lechi is wider than 3 it is permitted since the standing exceeds the breach (Riaz), but the view of Tosafos is that even so it is forbidden (Magen Avraham), and requires study:
9:_: [9] [Levush] Therefore, etc. And the Taz disagrees with Rama that from Terumat HaDeshen it appears specifically for tzurat hapetach where one need only one reed from here and one reed suffices in all that it is and not for lechi — and there is no difficulty, for Beit Yosef also holds that for every lechi all that it is suffices as above, and Levush Yom Tov wrote that Beit Yosef's view is that for every lechi all that it is suffices in any case; in smeared plaster he is uncertain, and it appears to me that for Rama it is obvious from broken fragments — until here, in She'arei Knesset HaGedolah it is explained that they practice even for lechi to be more lenient in smeared plaster for lechi than for tzurat hapetach, and they practice in both to be lenient, and it is obvious that the plaster should be somewhat thick like the cloak cord. Stones protruding from the fence one above the other less than 3 constitute a lechi when their combined height is 10 tefachim (Avodat HaKodesh):
10:_: [10] [Levush] If they kneaded, etc. So it is written in Beit Yosef, and I wonder that it was hidden from him the Mishnah at the end of Temurah and Yoreh De'ah siman 140 that ash of asheirah trees is forbidden in benefit — if so one must scatter it to the wind like the wood itself (Taz), and see siman 485 seif 3 and requires study; also it appears to me that commandments not to benefit were given and asheirah wood itself is forbidden as it stands to be burned and ash stands to be scattered to the wind in any case:
11:_: [11] [Levush] First form, second form, third form, fourth form. And for Chokhmat Shlomo the third form does not exist, for he wrote explicitly for all the world it does not exist (Levush Yom Tov), and see Taz and Nachalat Tzvi:
12:_: [12] [Levush] A tree that was planted, etc. And the same law if it grew by itself (Avodat HaKodesh):
13:_: [13] As if they leaned on it, etc. It appears that if explicitly they did not lean on it — such as they did not carry on the previous Shabbat through this lechi — it is not a lechi (Magen Avraham), and it appears to me specifically where they did not carry at all on the previous Shabbat when there was no other lechi there:
14:_: [14] [Levush] That the breach exceeds, etc. If the wall is more than 4 and we are uncertain whether it stands as half or majority over the breach — if it is not as breached it is permitted, for a doubt in their words is to be lenient, and furthermore there are two sides to be lenient: perhaps it is majority standing, and if you say it is not majority one can say perhaps like Avodat HaKodesh daf 5:
15:_: [15] And equal inside, etc. But in Tosafos daf 9 and Rosh they proved that in such a case it is not a lechi, for it is not called visible from outside except to those standing behind the mavo; but in truth Beit Yosef does not explain Tosafos and Rosh thus, and in any case Chokhmat Shlomo explained thus and so it appears (Levush Yom Tov):
16:_: [16] [Levush] For such is the law for every lechi, etc. Difficult from siman 365 seif 4, and one must say here he speaks of open to karmelis and requires study; and in Shulchan Aruch Magen Avraham wrote that the other side is shorter than this, and in the Gemara he speaks where the other side is also long — until here, and apparently for every lechi the other side is short and even so it is permitted and requires study:
17:_: [17] [Levush] And if it is 4 amot wide, etc. And the same law if he paved with lechayim less than less than 3 over a length of 4 amot, and specifically when the outer lechi does not protrude at all; but when it protrudes somewhat outside the mavo it is permitted. If they were distant from each other 3 tefachim one may use up to the outer end of the outer lechi, and if the entire lechi stands, etc. (Avodat HaKodesh daf 6):
18:_: [18] If he inserted, etc. Specifically when inserted within the thickness of the wall and protrudes outside; but at the wall it is permitted by reason of lechi (Olat Shabbat):
19:_: [19] To receive a brick, etc. Meaning if the mavo is 10 amot wide it must receive 18 bricks which is 9 amot as written in seif 25 (Avodat HaKodesh). Beit Yosef and Bach wrote: if made of straw and reeds even if strong enough to receive a brick it is forbidden since most straw and reeds are not strong. A mavo open on two sides that was repaired on one side with tzurat hapetach and on one side the two sides of the mavo were not equal but one short and one long — lechi suffices (Ralbag 66):
20:_: [20] A tefach and not in length 3 tefachim, etc. For then the korah is as lavud as written in seif 25, and likewise if there is a tefach it is as a korah — see there:
21:_: [21] There are those who say one needs, etc. So ruled Rambam and Semag, and so ruled in Avodat HaKodesh, and in Shiltei Giborim it appears this is the view of Rif:
22:_: [22] And it does not touch, etc. Even distant from the two walls — such as he inserted a reed of all that it is in the middle of the mavo to place a korah on it — for we say lavud from two sides (first chapter of Eruvin):
23:_: [23] And there are those who say one needs, etc. So it is written in Shulchan Aruch and Beit Yosef, and in my humble opinion those who say do not disagree with the first reason — that if together they have the width of a tefach it is permitted whenever between them is less than 3; but when together they have only half a tefach width then between them should be only a tefach so one can place on them a brick which is a tefach and a half — then one finger is placed on each korah; and although for korah only a tefach is needed, here where the two korot themselves lack a tefach and a tefach between them, two korot are needed, and so appears to me the explanation of Tur and R' Yehonatan, and so is proven in Avodat HaKodesh daf 5 and it is clear; also Bach and later authorities did not go into this, and what Bach was strict about — that specifically together they must have the width of a tefach and touch each other literally — is not so implied in the poskim, and so Nachalat Tzvi disagrees with him:
24:_: [24] Within a tefach. And even if together they are 4 — if the air between them is 4 tefachim it does not help, for in any case it is not fit to place a brick on them, unlike in seif 14 where it is fit only that they are not strong (Magen Avraham), and it appears to me there is a scribal error in his words and it must say if the air between them is more than a tefach it does not help — but understand; however I already wrote to be lenient whenever together they have the width of a tefach if between them is not 3 tefachim:
25:_: [25] And there are those who disqualify, etc. And we rule stringently (Bach):
26:_: [26] A korah wide, etc. Explanation: wide 10 tefachim — since it hangs 10 tefachim it leaves the category of korah like a machatzlet and it is a partition under which goats pass through and is forbidden as Rashba wrote; it teaches us it is permitted since the korah is visible and is not covered by a machatzlet — there a korah is on it. And what he wrote even if it extends below 10, etc. — we would have thought since it hangs below 10 from the ground there is no category of korah on it as he concludes. And what the Taz wondered on Rashba from seif 12 — it appears to me there is no difficulty, for in a partition more recognition is needed than for lechi:
27:_: [27] Spaced, etc. And at the end constricted — for we go stringently:
28:_: [28] Except with tzurat hapetach, etc. And Rambam: less than 4 amot its law is as a courtyard, and it is possible he did not mean tzurat hapetach specifically (Magen Avraham), and it appears to me that also in width of 10 amot and above its law is as a courtyard, and Shulchan Aruch and Levush relied on the amah he wrote at the end of the seif: or a pas, etc., or tzurat hapetach, and so appears in Avodat HaKodesh daf 4; also Magen Avraham omitted what is written in Shulchan Aruch seif 32:
29:_: [29] [Levush] That it does not hang, etc. And if the korah is 4 wide and strong to receive plaster it is permitted and not because of recognition but because the edge of the ceiling descends and closes — as long as the opening of the mavo is not more than 10; and so it appears to me that if it were 7 wide even if not strong it is valid since whenever it is 4 wide the eye dominates over it — Avodat HaKodesh 4:
30:_: [30] Building, etc. And the same with earth, and one must be careful when trampled by feet that it not diminish from the measure:
31:_: [31] Until they are open, etc. Rama's gloss was omitted and even all courtyards open to each other, and there are those who disagree — until here, and perhaps the reason is Beit Yosef ruled as those who disagree and stam is as his explanation that they are not open to each other (Levush Yom Tov), and one may wonder on one as great as him that he did not see at the end of this seif Levush wrote Rama's words as they are also for the law — the main thing is as the first view as Bach wrote, and likewise regarding houses open to each other; and in Avodat HaKodesh daf 4 even if each house and house made eruv, each house must have 4 amot by 4 amot or more:
32:_: [32] That its length exceeds, etc. And even all that it is (Avodat HaKodesh). Which is the length of the mavo — the way of its entrance; and what is not the way of entrance refers to its width, even though its width exceeds its length (there). The gloss Rama wrote here — Levush wrote at the end of this siman, and Levush Yom Tov erred in this and thought it was omitted to expand, and it is for nothing:
33:_: [33] That there is not in it 4, etc. Explanation: in its opening even if inside it is wide 4 (Beit Yosef), and so appears from R' Yehuda daf 92; R' Yehuda wrote daf 88 and specifically in a mavo but in a courtyard always needs repair — and see s.k. 3:
34:_: [34] [Levush] That one of its sides, etc. Explanation: its bank is 10 high, and specifically that it be literally adjacent to the head of the mavo; but if the river is distant from the houses 10 amot repair is needed for that place is breached, and likewise regarding refuse he speaks where it is 10 high; and it appears from Beit Yosef that even if one side sea and one side refuse and one side closed and one side open to reshut harabbim — lechi or korah is also permitted per this reasoning; and Levush wrote one of its sides to teach that there are those who say even so it needs repair. Emunat Shmuel siman 40 wrote: a city where a ditch 10 deep and 4 wide surrounds it is as a partition:
35:_: [35] And there are those who say, etc. And so is the main ruling, and so Bach ruled; and Magen Avraham wrote specifically regarding the sea but regarding other rivers we are not concerned lest a sandbar rise unless their way is to dry greatly in summer; and if they freeze in rainy season the partition is nullified and it is forbidden to carry, and the Taz expanded that since their way is to freeze they are forbidden forever, and in the Gemara he speaks of the sea whose way is not to freeze; and see Magen Avraham siman 365 s.k. 9:
36:_: [36] [Levush] And they will carry from the mavo, etc. This is the language of Levush Yom Tov — so Beit Yosef wrote in the name of Maggid Mishneh; but Rashi explained they will carry in the mavo itself, and Beit Yosef and Levush omitted Rashi's explanation; and it appears to me the Maggid does not explain that the entire side is sea and also not in width more than 10, therefore he was not concerned about carrying in the mavo itself — until here. And it appears to me the Maggid's view: even though dry land with a slope 10 deep remains as a partition as written at the end of this siman, nevertheless it is forbidden lest they carry from the mavo to karmelis; and so appears from Magen Avraham; but why he wrote that for Maggid Mishneh tzurat hapetach or lechi or korah does not help — only a complete partition — and in my humble opinion it helps since there is recognition they will not come to carry:
